---
name: luke-tests-need-node-24
description: Luke repo needs the newest installed Node 24.x — Node 22 cancels tests, and a missing 24.x patch makes check.sh compile Node from source
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 1555dd78-7b0d-4054-a738-1029939f9a9f
  modified: 2026-08-19T23:24:13.859Z
---

Two separate Node traps in the Luke repo, both hit through `./scripts/check.sh`.

**Tests cancel under Node 22.** `realtime-session.test.ts` reports 99
`cancelledByParent` failures ("Promise resolution is still pending but the event
loop has already resolved") under Node 22, even though `package.json` engines
says `>=22.12.0`. They pass 100% under Node 24 — the failures look like real
breakage but are environmental.

**`check.sh` will compile Node from source if the newest 24.x is missing.**
`scripts/oxlint.sh:15` runs `nvm install` unconditionally, and `.nvmrc` says
just `24`, so nvm resolves it to the *newest* 24.x release rather than accepting
any already-installed 24.x. On 2026-08-19 only v24.11.1 was installed, nvm
wanted v24.19.0, and it tried to build V8 from source — a ~10 minute detour that
then died on `No space left on device` (the data volume sits around 98% full).
The failure output is pages of clang warnings and looks nothing like a Node
version problem.

**Why:** both make a clean docs-only change look broken, and the second one's
error output points at V8 rather than at nvm.

**How to apply:** before `./scripts/check.sh` or `./scripts/verify.sh`, install
whatever `.nvmrc` currently resolves to and use it — `nvm install && nvm use`, or
check `nvm version-remote 24` against `ls ~/.nvm/versions/node/` first. Don't
just put an older 24.x on PATH; `oxlint.sh` re-resolves `.nvmrc` itself and will
start the source build regardless of what you exported. A full pass takes 10-20
minutes, so run it backgrounded rather than under a foreground timeout.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIRECTORY=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/workspace.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIRECTORY/lib/workspace.sh"

sidecar_require_macos
sidecar_require_node
sidecar_ensure_dependencies

# Running this script means "launch the build I just made", so an already-running
# instance is replaced rather than left in place. `--keep-running` opts out: the
# new launch then quits on startup and only re-asserts the running panel. Every
# other argument is forwarded to Electron.
replace_running_app=true
remaining_arguments=$#
while ((remaining_arguments-- > 0)); do
    argument=$1
    shift
    if [[ $argument == --keep-running ]]; then
        replace_running_app=false
        continue
    fi
    set -- "$@" "$argument"
done

if [[ $replace_running_app == true ]]; then
    sidecar_stop_running_app
fi

# Live sessions are the default. Pass `--fixture smoke` for deterministic data;
# the app honours it on its own, so nothing needs injecting here.
cd "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT"
exec pnpm start -- "$@"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIRECTORY=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
# shellcheck source=scripts/lib/workspace.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIRECTORY/lib/workspace.sh"

required_files=(
    AGENTS.md
    design/check-design-contract.mjs
    CHANGELOG.md
    CLAUDE.md
    docs/WORKFLOW.md
    README.md
    package.json
    pnpm-lock.yaml
    pnpm-workspace.yaml
    biome.json
    .nvmrc
    .husky/pre-commit

git -C "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT" diff --check

# The Node major is stated in more than one place because different readers look
# in different files, so they have to agree. `.nvmrc` is what local shells and
# CI read — the workflows name it as `node-version-file` — and Vercel reads
# neither it nor the root manifest: it takes `engines.node` from the deployed
# app and overrides its own dashboard setting with it. A stale `engines`
# therefore fails nothing and announces nothing local, and quietly ships
# production on a major no test ever ran on, which is how `22.x` outlived the
# move to 24. `.nvmrc` is the source; every declared major is checked against it.
nvmrc_major=$(sed -E 's/^v?([0-9]+).*$/\1/' "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/.nvmrc" | head -1)
engines_drift=""
for manifest in "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/package.json" \
    "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT"/apps/*/package.json \
    "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT"/packages/*/package.json; do
    declared=$(node -e 'const n = require(process.argv[1]).engines?.node; if (n) process.stdout.write(n)' \
        "$manifest")
    if [[ -z "$declared" ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    declared_major=$(printf '%s' "$declared" | grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1)
    if [[ "$declared_major" != "$nvmrc_major" ]]; then
        engines_drift+="${manifest#"$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/"}: engines.node \"$declared\" is not Node $nvmrc_major"$'\n'
    fi
done
if [[ -n "$engines_drift" ]]; then
    printf 'error: every engines.node must name the Node major .nvmrc pins (%s):\n%s' \
        "$nvmrc_major" "$engines_drift" >&2
    exit 1
fi

# it: the SVGs, the face the renderer draws, and the motions it plays. If the
# copies no longer match the source, one of them is telling a story the artwork

sidecar_nvmrc_node_major() {
    sed -E 's/^v?([0-9]+).*$/\1/' "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/.nvmrc" | head -1
}

# nvm's runtime is chosen per shell and shadowed by anything earlier on PATH, so
# a shell that never ran `nvm use` reaches these scripts on whatever Node it
# happens to have — and pnpm then runs every workspace under an engine none of
# them declare. Selecting `.nvmrc` here is what keeps the scripts usable from
# such a shell instead of leaving the caller to read a warning and guess.
sidecar_use_nvmrc_node() {
    local nvm_directory="${NVM_DIR:-$HOME/.nvm}"
    if [[ ! -r "$nvm_directory/nvm.sh" ]]; then
        return 1
    fi

    # pnpm forwards npm's configured install prefix into lifecycle scripts, and
    # nvm refuses to select a runtime while that prefix is set. This process owns
    # the runtime selection, and nothing here installs global packages.
    unset npm_config_prefix
    export NVM_DIR="$nvm_directory"
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    source "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"

    local requested
    requested=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/.nvmrc")
    # `nvm use` resolves a bare major against the versions already installed;
    # `nvm install` resolves it against the newest release and builds Node from
    # source when that exact patch is missing, a ten-minute detour for a runtime
    # the machine may already satisfy. Install only when nothing local matches.
    nvm use "$requested" >/dev/null 2>&1 || nvm install "$requested" >/dev/null || return 1
    export PATH="$NVM_DIR/versions/node/$(nvm current)/bin:$PATH"
}

sidecar_require_node() {
    sidecar_require_command node
    sidecar_require_command pnpm

    local required_major
    required_major=$(sidecar_nvmrc_node_major)
    local satisfied='process.exit(Number(process.versions.node.split(".")[0]) >= Number(process.argv[1]) ? 0 : 1)'

    if ! node -e "$satisfied" "$required_major"; then
        sidecar_use_nvmrc_node || true
    fi

    if ! node -e "$satisfied" "$required_major"; then
        printf 'error: Node.js %s or newer is required (found %s); install it with `nvm install` in %s\n' \
            "$required_major" "$(node --version)" "$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

local requested selected
    requested=$(tr -d '[:space:]' <"$SIDECAR_REPO_ROOT/.nvmrc")
    # `nvm version` resolves a bare major against the versions already installed,
    # where `nvm install` resolves it against the newest release and builds Node
    # from source when that exact patch is missing — a ten-minute detour for a
    # runtime the machine may already satisfy. Install only when nothing matches.
    selected=$(nvm version "$requested")
    if [[ $selected == N/A ]]; then
        nvm install "$requested" >/dev/null || return 1
        selected=$(nvm version "$requested")
    fi

    # Not `nvm use`: it edits the nvm entry already in PATH in place, so a Node
    # sitting ahead of that entry keeps winning and `nvm current` then reports
    # `system` for the very runtime it just selected. Prepending the resolved
    # version is what actually puts it in front.
    export PATH="$NVM_DIR/versions/node/$selected/bin:$PATH"
}

content.text:
Fixed. The warnings weren't a manifest problem — your shell's `node` is a Hermes-installed v22.23.1 at `~/.local/bin/node`, which sits ahead of nvm's `v24.19.0` on PATH, and the repo's own guard was stale.

**What was wrong**

- `sidecar_require_node` in `scripts/lib/workspace.sh:139` still demanded "22.18 or newer" while `.nvmrc` and every `engines.node` say 24. Node 22 sailed through the guard, and pnpm then warned on every workspace.
- `scripts/oxlint.sh` had the only nvm-selection code in the repo, and it was broken on this machine two ways: `nvm install` re-resolved the bare `24` against the *newest release* (the source-build trap), and `nvm use` + `nvm current` silently no-op'd — nvm edits the `~/.nvm/.../bin` entry already sitting at position 21 of your PATH in place, so `~/.local/bin/node` kept winning and `nvm current` reported `system` for the version it had just selected.

**Changes**

- `scripts/lib/workspace.sh` — the guard now derives the required major from `.nvmrc` (already the declared source of truth in `repository-checks.sh:81`), and when the current Node falls short it selects the `.nvmrc` runtime itself: resolves with `nvm version` against what's *installed*, installs only if nothing matches, and prepends the resolved path rather than trusting `nvm use`. Failure now names the version and how to get it.
- `scripts/oxlint.sh` — its private copy of the nvm dance is gone; `sidecar_require_node` covers it.
- `scripts/repository-checks.sh` — uses the shared `sidecar_nvmrc_node_major` instead of a second `sed` of `.nvmrc`.

**Verified**

- `./scripts/run.sh` — no engine warnings; native helpers built, bundles built, Electron is running (pid 87659). It replaced the instance that was running out of your `conductor/remote-workspace-sync` worktree, as `run.sh` is meant to.
- `./scripts/check.sh` — exit 0, 717 desktop tests, 0 failures, zero "Unsupported engine" lines. No UI change, so `verify.sh` isn't the invariant here.

Side effect worth knowing: `check.sh` now runs under Node 24 automatically, so the `realtime-session.test.ts` cancellation failures you'd get from a Node 22 shell won't recur either.
